notes: Capture the Flag as a Slayer game mode, rewritten as host rules: flags stand on Flag Spawn bricks in their team's colour; take an enemy flag to your own flag or a Flag Return Point to score; enough captures win the round; dropped flags go home after a while; /dropFlag drops a carried flag. Its brick events (onFlagPickedUp, onFlagDropped, onFlagReturned, onFlagRecovered) are in the wrench for builders to wire. So is the DropFlag output, which makes the player a row aims at drop the flag they carry. The flag waves where it stands and rides on the carrier's back in their team colour. Its settings are with Slayer's in the Mini-Game window's Add-On Settings, shown when the game mode is Capture the Flag. The Drop Tool key with the tools put away drops the flag too, a dropped flag counts down the seconds until it goes home over itself in its team's colour, and the carried flag glows in its team's colour. Slayer's setTeamControlLocked output locks a flag or Flag Return Point for a team: they cannot take that flag, or return flags there. A carried flag is no other Add-On's to swap or take off, a Flag Spawn whose item the wrench changes gets its flag back, and changing the game mode to or from Capture the Flag puts the flags on their stands or takes them away at once, with the captures. The End of Round Report shows Flag Pick-ups and Flag Returns where Slayer shows kills and deaths. A Flag Spawn or Flag Return Point planted or repainted tells its builder whose it is ("Flag Spawn set for Red."), and with Restrict Output Events on, only the game's editors may add DropFlag rows. Slayer's bots fill Capture the Flag teams as they do any team's. Bots with objective behavior can plan an eligible flag pickup and return through this package's explicit desired-state description; ordinary item contact, the carried flag image and actual return policy determine progress and wins. Plans are bounded and revalidate game, team, actor life and source incarnation; unknown policy semantics remain unsupported. Every paint colour has its own flag, so Max Flag Colors (how many flag colours the original made at start-up) has nothing to limit. Every flag type the copy declares is a choice in the host's Flag Type setting (Admin menu); flags on their stands change to it, and a carried flag keeps its look until it goes home.
